title: New ransomware campaign targeting cloud infrastructure
description: Security researchers have identified a new ransomware variant specifically designed to target cloud-based infrastructure. The campaign uses compromised CI/CD pipelines to deploy malicious code.

ai_analysis.impact_assessment: The ransomware campaign targeting cloud infrastructure can lead to significant disruptions, including data loss, service outages, and financial damages. recommended_actions: Implement strict access controls and monitor CI/CD pipelines for unusual activity.
Regularly back up critical data and ensure backups are stored in isolated environments.
Deploy endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions to identify and mitigate ransomware threats early.

title: Use of an insecure cryptographic algorithm in the cashless payment system using NFC wristbands...
description: Use of an insecure cryptographic algorithm in the cashless payment system using NFC wristbands from CasfID Servicios Tecnológicos S.L.U. (version used at Resurrection Fest 2025), which employs cards based on MIFARE Classic technology (FM11RF08S). The cryptographic weakness of the authentication algorithm allows an attacker to retrieve access keys using techniques known as Backdoored Nested Attack, read the wristband’s entire contents, and clone its credentials onto a compatible rewritable card.

ai_analysis.impact_assessment: The use of an insecure cryptographic algorithm in NFC wristbands could lead to unauthorized access, credential cloning, and financial fraud. Attackers can exploit this vulnerability to compromise the integrity of cashless payment systems, potentially causing reputational damage and financial losses.
recommended_actions: Upgrade to a more secure cryptographic algorithm, such as AES-based encryption, and discontinue the use of MIFARE Classic technology.
Implement additional layers of authentication and encryption to secure NFC communications.
Conduct a security audit of all systems using NFC wristbands and educate users about potential risks.

title: A Path Traversal vulnerability exists in Quick.CMS through the URI path component of HTTP...
description:
A Path Traversal vulnerability exists in Quick.CMS through the URI path component of HTTP requests, where the server fails to normalize dot-dot-slash (../) sequences before resolving and serving the requested file. An authenticated attacker with admin privileges can use this vulnerability to read contents of files located in the sibling directory of the webroot via a crafted HTTP request containing ../ sequences in the URI.


The vendor assessed the likelihood of exploitation as very low and det

ai_analysis.impact_assessment: The vulnerability allows an authenticated attacker with admin privileges to access sensitive files outside the webroot directory, potentially exposing configuration files, sensitive data, or credentials stored on the server. However, the likelihood of exploitation is low due to the requirement of admin-level access.
recommended_actions: Update Quick.CMS to the latest version if a patch is available or apply vendor-recommended mitigations.
Restrict admin account access to trusted users and enforce strong authentication mechanisms such as multi-factor authentication (MFA).
Implement web server configurations to restrict access to sensitive files and directories outside the webroot.

title: Quick.CMS is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion (LFI) in the admin.php endpoint via the p...
description:
Quick.CMS is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion (LFI) in the admin.php endpoint via the p parameter. An authenticated attacker with admin privileges can include arbitrary files located within the application's directory structure via a crafted HTTP request. Successful exploitation allows disclosure of the server's directory structure and absolute file paths (path disclosure).



The vendor assessed the likelihood of exploitation as very low and determined that a fix is not necessary.

title: CVE-2026-55833 - Netty is a network application framework for development of protocol servers and clients. Prior to 4
description: Netty is a network application framework for development of protocol servers and clients. Prior to 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, Netty SPDY header decoding continues inflating zlib-compressed header blocks after the raw header parser has exceeded `maxHeaderSize` and marked the frame truncated in `SpdyFrameCodec`, allowing a remote peer to send a small compressed `HEADERS` block that expands into much larger raw header data and causes compression-amplified CPU and allocation churn. This issue is fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.

title: CVE-2026-55831 - Netty is a network application framework for development of protocol servers and clients. Prior to 4
description: Netty is a network application framework for development of protocol servers and clients. Prior to 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, Netty's SPDY SETTINGS decoder accepts a peer-declared SETTINGS entry count up to the 24-bit frame-length limit and materializes every unique setting ID in `DefaultSpdySettingsFrame`, allowing a remote SPDY/3.1 peer to send a syntactically valid roughly 2 MiB SETTINGS frame that creates 262144 map entries and amplifies network input into heap growth and ordered-map insertion work. This issue is fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
